business_problem: ATP needed to keep mission-critical, service-centric platforms running at high speed and in compliance with local regulations while improving DevOps efficiency, redundancy, and scalability for client-facing systems across finance, hospitality, and energy.
solution_summary: ATP built a cloud-native operating model on Alibaba Cloud so it could run customer-facing platforms with stronger automation and resilience. Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) became the primary runtime for the company's core systems, simplifying deployment and scaling of containerized services that connect directly with enterprise customers. Elastic Compute Service supplies the underlying compute backbone, while Server Load Balancer provides the entry layer that keeps traffic distributed across healthy services. NAT Gateway supports controlled outbound connectivity for the environment, and Simple Log Service centralizes operational visibility so ATP's teams can troubleshoot and tune systems without adding manual overhead. This stack supports the company's service-centric architecture for workloads that process thousands of orders per second and must comply with local requirements. In practice, Alibaba Cloud gives ATP a more repeatable DevOps foundation for regulated, high-throughput enterprise software delivery.
business_outcome: ATP improved scalability, redundancy, and operational efficiency for its enterprise platforms while preserving the compliance posture required by its regulated customers.

solution_components.name: Server Load Balancer

solution_components.name: NAT Gateway
solution_components.role: Handles controlled network egress for workloads running inside ATP's cloud environment.

data_flow: Client requests enter through Server Load Balancer, are processed by containerized services on ACK backed by Elastic Compute Service, and emit operational telemetry to Simple Log Service while NAT Gateway manages controlled network connectivity.
